query: How do review facets differ by sentiment label?

per_column.name: review_word_count
per_column.rationale: Length is a mildly informative facet that can differ by sentiment; derivable directly from text. Somewhat generic but gives a groupable axis.

per_column.name: review_sentence_count
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with word count and generic structural metric; still soundly derived from text.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation intensity is a genuine stylistic facet plausibly linked to sentiment; trivially extractable and values match text.

per_column.name: question_count
per_column.rationale: Rhetorical questions can mark negative/critical reviews; well grounded (row 1 and 3 questions counted correctly).

per_column.name: caps_word_count
per_column.rationale: All-caps emphasis is a plausible sentiment-linked facet; mostly grounded though 'REAL' title vs content scope makes some counts ambiguous.

per_column.name: positive_word_count
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to sentiment facet analysis and gives comparative leverage; lexicon-based so somewhat dependent on word list but readings are reasonable.

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Strong axis for contrasting facets by sentiment; row 3 (clearly negative text) counted 0 negative words shows lexicon limits, but generally sound.

per_column.name: has_personal_pronoun
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (203/47) and generic; adds little discriminating leverage though accurately extracted.

per_column.name: avg_word_length
per_column.rationale: Low-variance stylistic metric with weak link to sentiment facets; correctly computable from text.

judge.rationale: The added columns are all extractive/computable facets soundly derived from the review text, with no invented facts (values in row samples match the source). For the query about how facets differ by sentiment, the sentiment-lexicon and punctuation columns provide genuine analytical axes, while several structural metrics (sentence count, avg word length, personal pronoun flag) are generic, low-variance, or redundant, dragging holistic usefulness to moderate. Groundedness is high overall; the only soft spots are lexicon-based sentiment counts that occasionally miss clearly negative rows (e.g., row 3), but these are reasonable readings rather than hallucinations.
